newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Last foreign aid workers leave east Zaire city.
newsitem.headline: Last foreign aid workers leave east Zaire city.

text.p: The last seven foreign aid workers left the beleaguered east Zairean city of Bukavu by plane on Monday as mortar and machinegun fire blasted to the south.
Zairean aid staff said the foreign aid workers told them they were leaving only when they arrived at the airport. Zairean troops quickly moved to their compound and looted computers and telephones.
Staff said the departing aid workers told their Zairean employees to go back to their homes and lock themselves in.

The seven were from the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), the International Federation of Red Cross and Red Crescent Societies (IFRC), the Belgian Red Cross and World Health Organisation.
They were to be flown to Nairobi, Kenya, local staff said, adding their departure meant no other foreign aid workers remained in the city.

Heavy gunfire, from mortars and machineguns, erupted about five km (three miles) south and southwest of the city shortly after the seven left, after telling journalists at their hotel they were going to visit a hospital.
The aid workers told local ICRC and IFRC staff they were leaving when they arrived at the airport north of Bukavu.
"It's terrible for them not to tell us. Of course it makes us panic. Of course the military will come and take the cars," said an ICRC employee, after hearing a radio message that they had left.
Most foreign aid workers were evacuated by air from Bukavu to Nairobi on Saturday after unruly Zairean troops stole aid agency vehicles and robbed foreigners as Tutsi rebels advanced.

Fifteen Belgians and other foreigners, including children clutching teddy bears, earlier on Monday left Bukavu on a flight organised by the Belgian embassy. They were escorted to the airport by troops.

Soldiers kept looting on Monday but a new Zairean military governor, who arrived the same day, tried to create a semblance of discipline. Some soldiers loyal to him tried to stop some of the robberies by other troops from expatriate and Zairean homes.

At one point soldiers set up a checkpoint in Bukavu city and turned back troops trying to pass with loot. Some witnesses said a number of soldiers were arrested but it was unclear if the clampdown would work as Tutsi rebels pushed closer to the city.
